newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Weather seen favouring Ukraine beet harvest.
newsitem.headline: Weather seen favouring Ukraine beet harvest.

text.p: Warm weather forecast for much of this month should spur Ukraine's sugar harvest, which began two weeks late to allow beets to grow larger, industry officials said on Monday.
"There will be dry, warm weather until the end of October, which will help with the gathering of Ukraine's harvests," said Mykolae Kulbida, head of the Weather Forecasting Centre.
"We don't exclude the fact that in the last few days of October there may be cold temperatures and even frosts, but we don't envisage winter beginning this month."
The government has forecast a poor beet harvest of 26 million tonnes, down from last year's 30 million.
"All hopes of sugar producers are pinned on the weather forecast," Leonid Bershtein, a deputy director of Ukraine's Sugar Research Institute, said.
He said about 250,000 hectares of beets had been harvested out of a total of 1.306 million ha, adding, "The harvest really started on October 1."
Olexander Bohatarenyk, deputy head of the state concern Ukrtsukor, said that the pace of the harvest and delivery of beets to refineries had increased in the last few days.
"More than 100 refineries have started processing beets," Bohatarenyk said, adding that more than 150,000 tonnes of sugar had been processed from 1.8 million tonnes of beets.
"The one thing that is worrying us is that if we have frosts in the last half of October, there will be significant losses in production," he said.
Government forecasts put refined sugar output this year at 2.8 to 3.0 million tonnes, down from last year's nearly 3.5 million tonnes.
The Agriculture Ministry said last week that the beet harvest was experiencing big delays due to chronic fuel shortages, and a deputy prime minister blamed equipment breakdowns.
There are 191 sugar refineries in Ukraine and one refinery-research centre.
